small_guidance:
- The kernel re-loads each input element POOL*POOL times per (kh,kw); reorder the inner loops so the POOL×POOL accumulation reuses x_val in registers — load x once for (in_h,in_w) and accumulate against the relevant weight neighbors, or swap so (kh,kw) is the innermost loop and POOL×POOL is outermost with x cached.
- Add `triton.autotune` over BLOCK_P ∈ {64,128,256,512}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3}; current BLOCK_P=256 with PH*PW=9216 may be suboptimal — try smaller blocks with more programs to improve occupancy on the 4090.
- Eliminate the atomic_add by tiling so one program owns the full (n,oc) reduction (persistent loop over p tiles) and writes a single value to out_partial[n,oc]; this removes contention across the (P_total/BLOCK_P) atomics per (n,oc).
large_guidance:
- Redesign as im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, OC-tile, pool-output-tile), with the GEMM-K dimension being IC*KH*KW. Accumulate into a [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_P*POOL*POOL] tile (or fold the POOL×POOL average into the epilogue by accumulating sums across the 4×4 sub-window in registers), then sigmoid and reduce to a scalar per (n, oc-tile) — sum dim=[1,2,3] gets fused entirely, no atomics, no out_partial.
- Use channels_last (NHWC) input layout so the GEMM-K (IC×KH×KW) loads are contiguous; pre-permute x once in forward. This is the dominant bandwidth win since IC=8 is tiny and current NCHW layout forces strided reads.
- Make the kernel persistent over (n, oc) with each program reducing its full spatial extent into a single fp32 register, then a final small kernel (or torch.sum) reduces across oc. This collapses the 9216-element intermediate into registers and avoids the global atomic_add bottleneck entirely.
